AccountView.description:
One account the login screen can offer, so a visitor does not have to be
told which username shows what.
AccountView.title: AccountView

ChangeOrderView.description: One variation the contractor has proposed, priced against the signed BoQ.
ChangeOrderView.title: ChangeOrderView

LoanSummaryView.description:
The loan itself — what every owner and bank header needs to name it.

Deliberately not screen-shaped: it carries the loan's own facts, and each
screen picks the subset it renders.
LoanSummaryView.title: LoanSummaryView

LoginRequest.description:
A username and a password, resolved against either mechanism.

Either one of the three provisioned accounts plus the shared demo password,
or an account somebody created through sign-up plus their own. The caller
does not say which, and cannot: the answer decides the role.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

NewChangeOrder.description:
What the owner types when they log a change their contractor has asked for
verbally. `neevs_read` is deliberately absent: the read is Neev's, and a
caller that could write it could put words in the product's mouth.
NewChangeOrder.title: NewChangeOrder

PhaseHistoryView.description:
One build phase, after the fact: claimed, seen, decided.

Read by both Build Progress (the owner's account of their build) and Tranche
Decision (the lender's audit trail), from one mapper, so the two cannot tell
different stories about the same phase.
PhaseHistoryView.title: PhaseHistoryView

SignupRequest.description:
Everything needed to open an account and the loan behind it.

The loan fields are here rather than on a later screen because a borrower
with no loan has nothing to be shown: every owner screen reads
`/api/loans/{id}`. A brand-new loan answers 200 with no tranches and no
revisions, and the screens render that as "nothing checked yet".
SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest

info.description: Serves pipeline-shaped loan data to the Neev owner and bank consoles.
info.title: Neev API

get.description:
Which accounts exist, for the login screen's own hint list.

Usernames only. No password, and nothing about the loans behind them beyond
the label a visitor needs to choose.

schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Auth Accounts Get

get.description: Bank-only: this is the lender's private view of its own builders.
Why a run failed, for a client that missed the stream's error event.
Every variation on this loan, with the running total underneath.

post.description:
Log a change the contractor asked for off the record.

Tone is `neutral` and the read says plainly that the owner logged it: a
figure Neev never checked must not arrive wearing the same warn/danger
colours as one it did.

Accept, decline or counter one change order.

A lender may read this loan's variations but never answer them: the reply is
the borrower's decision about their own contract.

A borrower reporting progress: a stage, some photos, an optional note.

The photos attach to the tranche currently under review, which is the one
whose release they are evidence for.

Every field this endpoint cannot actually establish is left null: the
geotag, timestamp and same-angle flags, which the visual inspector fills in
live mode, and `taken_at` — upload time is not capture time, and writing it
into an evidence trail as though it were would be the one lie a verification
record cannot afford.

get.description:
One photograph from this loan's evidence.

Loan-scoped on purpose: `AuthorizedLoan` lets a lender read any loan in the
book and an owner only their own, and the photo is looked up *within* the
authorized loan rather than by id alone — otherwise any signed-in borrower
could walk the id space and read another family's site photographs.

Private and immutable: the bytes never change once written, but they are
somebody's home under construction, so this is `private` rather than
`public` and never lands in a shared cache.

post.description:
Marks the drafted questions sent.

Idempotent: a second click does not re-stamp `sent_at` on a question already
sent, and the count returned is how many questions are now with the
contractor — the number the screen says it sent, both times.

Only the questions the screen actually showed are stamped. The BoQ Review
panel ranks and caps the list (see `mappers.boq.visible_questions`), and the
WhatsApp message the owner sends carries exactly those — so stamping the
whole stored list would record eighteen questions as "sent" that nobody
ever sent.

get.description:
The officer's view of one tranche. Bank-only: it carries the officer's
narrative alongside the borrower's.

post.description:
Append an audit event and update the latest-state projection atomically.

Clients can deduplicate retries using Idempotency-Key. Reusing a key with a
different payload is a conflict; an unkeyed submission is a new decision.
